evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-13"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-13". POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is a plain YYYY-MM-DD value with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 with {"dueDate":"2026-01-02"} returned 200 and the new date. PATCH with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null, so the date is changed and removed.
evidence.AC3: These all returned 400 with an error message: POST dueDate "2026-02-30", POST "14.10.2026", POST "2026-10-14T10:00:00Z", PATCH "2026-02-30", PATCH "nope".
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-14. Four todos were created: one due 10-13 (not done), one due today, one due 2026-12-01, and one with no due date. A fifth was due 2026-01-01 and then marked done. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the 10-13 todo. The responses' overdue flags were false for today's date, the future date, no date, and the done todo.
evidence.AC5: The page at / listed "fällig: 13.10.2026", "fällig: 14.10.2026", "fällig: 01.12.2026" and "fällig: 01.01.2026" next to the matching todos. The todo with no due date showed none.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot only the 10-13 todo carried the text "überfällig". The today, future, no-date and done-past todos did not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled "nur überfällige". Clicking it reduced the list to the single overdue todo, "past".
